# Limitations {#sec-limitations}

Every behavioural quantity in this paper is a share of conversations matched to tasks (@sec-data): it describes usage of one assistant on one platform, not the conduct of the people employed in an occupation. A high automation share for an occupation's tasks says that the conversations classified to those tasks were mostly of the automation kind, not how many people in that occupation use the model or how they divide their own work. The wording rule is therefore a substantive limit, binding RQ1 most, where H1–H4 relate usage shares to occupational wages, education, error costs and country income (@sec-rq1): the regressors describe occupations and countries, while the outcome describes only the conversations that reached the platform from them. Usage is also concentrated. In a post-result diagnostic (PAP §11 D-3; exploratory; not a decision), leaving out SOC major group {{< var diag.h1.leave_out_soc_major_15.dropped >}}, which carries {{< var diag.h1.leave_out_soc_major_15.dropped_weight_pct >}}% of the H1 weight, gives $\beta_w$ = {{< var diag.h1.leave_out_soc_major_15.beta_w >}} (p = {{< var diag.h1.leave_out_soc_major_15.p_w >}}) and $\beta_e$ = {{< var diag.h1.leave_out_soc_major_15.beta_e >}} (p = {{< var diag.h1.leave_out_soc_major_15.p_e >}}) (@tbl-diag-h1-influence; @sec-app-supplementary). The robustness rows that move the H1 coefficients most, R26 `gwa` and `dwa`, R24 r4 and r5, R24 `r6_1p_api` and R10 `ub`, are reported in @sec-robustness.

No AEI release names the model that classifies its conversations, and the platform scope widens across releases (@tbl-regimes; @sec-app-supplementary). A change in the classifier, or in the conversations it sees, between two releases cannot be distinguished from a change in how people work with the model; this is the first open risk of the data audit, which the published files cannot resolve (@sec-data). It bears on every comparison across releases, above all H2 and the exploratory, look-ahead `A_pooled` index, which averages releases measured under different regimes (@sec-rq2).

Within published tasks, AEI withholds cells below its thresholds; the primary measure renormalises over the classified patterns, and the R10 bounds count the suppressed mass as all automation or as none. Across occupations, the width of those bounds on the automation share has a median of {{< var rq2.bounds_occupation.automation.p50 >}} pp and an interquartile range of {{< var rq2.bounds_occupation.automation.p25 >}} to {{< var rq2.bounds_occupation.automation.p75 >}} pp over {{< var rq2.bounds_occupation.automation.n >}} occupations (@tbl-rq2-bounds-occupations; @sec-app-supplementary). Occupations with no AEI usage are a separate case: they are unpublished in AEI, not measured as zero, and are assigned zero by assumption (D3). Under Design B this covers {{< var audit.zero_assigned_pct.b >}}% of employment (@sec-data). The RQ2 correlations depend on that assumption, and R3, which drops those occupations instead, lowers them most (@sec-rq2).

Two further construction choices are equal splits that use no employment information. A task statement shared by several occupations gives each an equal part of its usage (D4): this keeps the usage numerator independent of its employment denominator but produces dispersion within groups of related occupations that share tasks, an open risk of the data audit (@sec-data). The pre-registered alternative, R11, splits by employment, which removes the dispersion by construction rather than measuring how much of it is an artefact (@sec-robustness). Likewise, the NAICS-to-FF49 concordance splits a NAICS code equally over its SIC codes (D23), so the industry weights are structural rather than employment-based, a departure from the spec's employment-weighted crosswalk (PAP §10.2), which is row R33 (@sec-robustness). The same OEWS occupation-to-industry weights enter both sides of every RQ2 comparison, so part of each correlation is common occupational mix (@sec-rq2).

The time dimension of H2 is four release cross-sections, r2 to r5 (@sec-methods). Under task fixed effects the trend is identified only across releases, which is why the release-level wild bootstrap is a co-condition. The measured within-task trend is {{< var rq1.h2.beta >}} pp per year, but H2 is {{< var rq1.h2.decision_text >}}: the release-level co-condition fails at {{< var rq1.holm.h2 >}} (@sec-rq1). The rise is one r2 to r3 step followed by a fall (@fig-rq1-h2-release-effects). Leaving out r2 reverses the sign of β, to {{< var diag.h2.leave_out_release_r2.beta >}} pp per year, in the post-result diagnostic of PAP §11 D-3 (exploratory; not a decision; @tbl-diag-h2-influence; @sec-app-supplementary). The r2 to r3 step coincides with the change in the classified-conversation base, so classifier or platform drift cannot be separated from behaviour, and R22 `api_r3_r5` and R23 run the other way (@sec-robustness). The balanced panel removes {{< var diag.h2.balancing_removed.n_tasks >}} tasks carrying {{< var diag.h2.balancing_removed.usage_share_pct >}}% of usage (descriptive; @tbl-diag-h2-influence).

The market test is a cross-section of {{< var design.n_industries >}} FF49 industries, and one of them dominates it. Design B delegation exposure places {{< var audit.exposure.b.z_del_max_industry >}} at {{< var audit.exposure.b.z_del_max >}} SD, against {{< var audit.exposure.b.z_del_2nd >}} SD for the next industry, and Softw's leverage is {{< var rq3.influence.softw.h5.leverage >}} in the H5 regression and {{< var rq3.influence.softw.h5b.leverage >}} in H5b (@tbl-rq3-influence-softw; @sec-app-supplementary). Its DFBETAS and Cook's distance on the slope are nonetheless small, and the R13 estimates lie close to the primaries; R12 (ranks) and R13 (dropping Softw) are co-primary for this reason, R13 with larger MDEs (@sec-markets).

The confirmatory returns span one {{< var design.window.months >}}-month window, {{< var design.window.start >}} to {{< var design.window.end >}}, a single draw of the cross-section of industry alphas, for which the H5 MDE of {{< var d11.primary_mde >}} pp per standard deviation exceeds the D11 threshold of {{< var design.plausibility_pp >}} pp (@sec-markets).

Design B is out of sample in AEI data only, not strictly real-time (S1). Its OEWS {{< var vintage.oews.primary >}} weights were released on {{< var design.s1.oews_release >}}, after the formation date of {{< var design.formation >}} and inside the return window, and its O*NET {{< var vintage.onet.primary >}} task links also postdate formation, although their task text matches {{< var vintage.onet.r32 >}} (PAP §11, C-74; @sec-app-deviations). R32 rebuilds the index from inputs public at formation (OEWS {{< var vintage.oews.r32 >}}, O*NET {{< var vintage.onet.r32 >}}), giving H5 and H5b slopes of {{< var rob.r32.h5.estimate >}} and {{< var rob.r32.h5b.estimate >}} pp per SD (@sec-app-robustness-tables); R1, on OEWS {{< var vintage.oews.r1 >}}, is look-ahead (@sec-robustness). R32 is a market row only, so no RQ2 correlation exists under strictly real-time inputs.

The seal kept code from reading industry returns dated on or after {{< var design.seal_date >}} until the protocol was tagged ({{< var pap.tag >}}, {{< var pap.date >}}), but it cannot remove what the researchers, or the language model assisting them, know from public commentary about broad market moves since then. The protection is procedural: the confirmatory test, its exposure vector, null values and script were frozen before any post-seal return was read, and Design A is exploratory for this reason (@sec-app-disclosures). Pre-tag choices were made with that knowledge; no procedure can show it left them untouched.

The H6 talk index counts filers whose 10-K filings EDGAR full-text search returns for a quoted phrase. Its matching semantics are those the SEC implemented on the retrieval date, which this paper does not control; the case, whitespace and hyphen rules bind only the secondary measure. Each filer's FF49 industry is its current SIC from the EDGAR submissions file retrieved at {{< var h6.vintage.submissions_retrieved_utc >}}, applied to every filing year, so both inputs are fixed at retrieval rather than in the filing year (@sec-markets). The secondary measure needed a correction to input data after results were seen, logged as deviation D-1 in PAP §11 (@sec-app-deviations): two truncated 10-K documents were fetched again. H6 is exploratory, and its sensitivity to single industries is the post-result leave-one-industry-out diagnostic (PAP §11 D-3; exploratory; not a decision; @tbl-diag-h6-influence; @sec-app-supplementary).
